cards.explanation: The answer is the key to the pit of the Abyss. John, who is seeing this vision, says the star "…was given the key to the pit of the Abyss." Notice the star is handed the key, like a manager handing over the shop keys at closing time.

The answer is True. The verse says "…the sun and the air were darkened by the smoke from the pit." The smoke rises like the smoke of a great furnace, and it's big enough to darken the sun. My worst batch only darkened my mood.

The answer is False. The locusts "…were told not to harm the grass of the earth or any plant or tree…" They're told to harm only those who did not have the seal of God on their foreheads. Real locusts would be eating the whole yard by now, but these ones get told something very different.

The answer is only those without God's seal on their foreheads. The locusts are told to harm "…only those who did not have the seal of God on their foreheads." The seal is the whole dividing line in this verse. Earlier in Revelation, God's servants are sealed on their foreheads too (Revelation 7:3).

The answer is False. The verse says the locusts "…were not given power to kill them, but only to torment them for five months…" It's a heavy part of the passage, and I won't pretend otherwise. The five months matter, because the time is set.

The missing word is "die." The text says, "In those days men will seek death and will not find it; they will long to die, but death will escape them." This is one of the heaviest lines in the passage. It tells how bad the torment is, since people long for death and can't find it.

The answer is horses prepared for battle. The verse says "…the locusts looked like horses prepared for battle…" Not just horses, but horses prepared for battle, friends. That's quite a picture to get from a bug.

The answer is True. John says the locusts "…had breastplates like breastplates of iron, and the sound of their wings was like the roar of many horses and chariots rushing into battle." So there's armor like iron, and a sound like horses and chariots rushing into battle. I think that's a lot to take in at once.

The answer is the angel of the Abyss. The locusts "…were ruled by a king, the angel of the Abyss." The verse gives his name in Hebrew and in Greek, and it's the same king either way. So these locusts answer to someone.

The missing word is "two." The verse says, "The first woe has passed. Behold, two woes are still to follow." The eagle cried woe three times (Revelation 8:13), so one is down and two are left. The story is still going.

The missing word is "altar." John says he heard "…a voice from the four horns of the golden altar before God". It's a golden altar, and it stands before God. The voice speaks to the sixth angel right after the trumpet sounds.
The answer is to kill a third of mankind. The four angels "…were released to kill a third of mankind." This is a heavy verse, and I think it hurts to read.

The answer is True. John says, "…the number of mounted troops was two hundred million; I heard their number." He says he heard the number, not that he counted it. Two hundred million is a number I'd want to hear twice.

The answer is the heads of lions. The verse says, "The heads of the horses were like the heads of lions…" The riders have breastplates the colors of fire, sapphire and sulfur, and the horses have heads like the heads of lions. That's a lot to take in at once.

The missing word is "snakes." The verse says, "…their tails were like snakes, having heads with which to inflict harm." The horses are dangerous at both ends, the mouths and the tails. I'll stay far away from the back end of any horse, thank you.

The answer is that they cannot see or hear or walk. John says the idols "…cannot see or hear or walk." These are idols of gold, silver, bronze, stone and wood. The verse says the rest of mankind still did not stop worshiping them.

The answer is False. The verse says, "Furthermore, they did not repent of their murder, sorcery, sexual immorality, and theft." That's a sad ending for this part of the story, friends, and the text doesn't soften it.
